header_title: The Falling Elevator Is the Universe
tagline: Weight and gravity are locally indistinguishable
question_text: Why can no experiment tell free fall from deep space?
audio_script: I am going to show you the thought experiment Einstein called his happiest. You are standing on a bathroom scale inside an elevator. The cable snaps. The elevator falls. In the first instant, the scale reads your weight. A fraction of a second later, it reads less. Then less. Then zero. What happened? Your mass did not change. Gravity still pulls on you exactly the same way. But you and the scale are both accelerating downward at g. There is no normal force left for the scale to measure. It reads zero because it has nothing to push against. Here is the strange part, and it is the seed of general relativity. The exact same scale reading, zero, could also be produced by removing you and the scale to deep space, far from any planet or star, and letting the whole apparatus drift. Free fall and weightlessness are locally indistinguishable. No experiment you can perform inside that falling room can tell you which one you are in. A pendulum hangs straight. A laser beam travels in a straight line. A dropped ball floats next to you. Every physical test gives the same answer. The word is local. If your body were the size of a planet, you could measure the tidal pull across your width. The top of your head would fall at a slightly different rate than your toes, and you would feel a stretching force. But for a small room in free fall, the physics inside is exactly the physics of empty space. This is why astronauts float on the space station. They are not far from Earth's gravity. They are falling around it, forever missing the ground. Inside their little falling room, no experiment can tell them whether they are at rest in the void or crashing toward a planet.

tagline: Every explosion has a still center
question_text: Where is the center of a spinning exploding object?
audio_script: I am going to show you a point that does not know an explosion has happened. Light a firework. It climbs. At the top of its arc it explodes into a hundred fragments. Every fragment flies off in its own direction. Every fragment follows its own parabola. The motion looks chaotic. Now watch a single point. The center of mass. Follow it through the explosion. It continues along exactly the same smooth path it would have followed if the firework had never exploded. It does not know the shell broke apart. It does not know a hundred pieces are flying. It keeps moving as if nothing happened. This is the deepest structural fact about many-body physics. Newton's second law applied to every atom separately is a nightmare of bookkeeping. Applied once to the center of mass, it becomes a single sentence. The net external force equals total mass times the acceleration of the center of mass. Internal forces cancel in pairs. They never move the center of mass. This is why a bullet and a rifle recoil together. Why a rocket accelerates even though the exhaust is pushing away from it. Why two ice skaters who push off each end up with the same center of mass they started with. A hundred particles, a thousand, a billion. The center of mass always behaves like a single particle carrying all the mass, driven only by the net external force. Every explosion has a still point. The center of mass knows nothing of chaos.

header_title: Blow Across a Sheet of Paper
tagline: Fast air pushes less. You would have guessed more.
question_text: Why does the paper rise?
audio_script: I am going to show you something that contradicts your intuition. Hold a sheet of paper by its edge. Blow across the top. The paper rises. Almost everyone expects it to sink, because you are blowing on it. It rises instead. Why? Moving air has lower pressure than still air at the same height. This is Bernoulli's principle, and it is one of the most counterintuitive facts in everyday physics. The reason is energy. A fluid element moving fast has more kinetic energy than one moving slowly. If nothing else is pushing energy into the fluid, then the pressure, which is a form of energy density, must drop to compensate. Pressure plus half rho v squared plus rho g h equals a constant along a streamline. Where the speed goes up, the pressure must go down. Watch this in a venturi tube. The pipe narrows. By continuity the fluid must speed up to get through. As the fluid speeds up, its pressure drops. You can see the pressure drop directly if you stick a small vertical tube into the narrow section. The fluid rises less than it does in the wide section, because the pressure pushing it up is smaller. Every atomizer, every carburetor, every chimney, every curveball, every airplane wing leans on this same fact. The air on the curved top of a wing moves faster than the air underneath, so the pressure up there is lower, and the wing is pushed upward. Not because the wing is being sucked up. Because the ordinary pressure underneath has no counterweight above it. Fast air, low pressure. Slow air, high pressure. It is that simple and that strange.

tagline: Action at a distance becomes local action
question_text: How does one charge know another is nearby?
audio_script: I am going to show you how one charge knows that another charge is nearby. It cannot see. It cannot shout. Yet if you bring two positive charges close together, they repel. Instantly. With no visible connection between them. Newton called this action at a distance, and he hated it. He thought it was the greatest absurdity in physics. Faraday found a way out, and it is one of the great conceptual shifts in the history of science. Instead of saying that one charge reaches across space and pulls on another, say that each charge creates something in the space around it. That something is the electric field. Picture a small positive test charge that you can carry around. At every point in space, the field tells you what force that test charge would feel. Near a positive charge, the field arrows point outward, like porcupine quills. Farther away, they thin out. Double the distance and each arrow gets four times weaker, because the field falls off as one over r squared. Now place a second charge in this field. It does not need to know that the first charge exists. It only feels the field at its own location, and it responds locally. The first charge creates the field. The field travels. The second charge responds. Action at a distance has been replaced by two local events, connected by a messenger. This is why the field concept survived from Faraday to Maxwell to Einstein. A charge never reaches across space. It only changes the space right around it.

tagline: Entropy counts arrangements
question_text: Why does heat flow one way and never the other?
audio_script: I am going to show you why you cannot un-stir coffee. Put a single drop of ink into a glass of water. Stir once. The ink spreads. It keeps spreading. After a minute it is evenly distributed through the glass. It stays that way. Now try to reverse it. Try to gather all the ink molecules back into a single concentrated drop, in one small corner of the glass. You cannot. Not because the laws of mechanics forbid it. Every collision between ink and water is reversible. If you ran the movie backwards, every collision would still obey Newton's laws. Nothing about the microscopic dynamics prefers one direction over the other. But the number of ways to arrange the ink molecules so that they are all in one corner is astronomically smaller than the number of ways to arrange them so that they are spread evenly. The system evolves toward the more numerous arrangements, not because it is forced to, but because it is overwhelmingly more likely. This is entropy. The second law of thermodynamics says that in an isolated system, entropy never decreases. Not because the reverse is forbidden. Because the reverse is so improbable that you would need to wait longer than the age of the universe to see it. The universe is not marching toward disorder. It is marching toward the most numerous arrangements. Almost all of them look disordered to us.

tagline: Step through the two conservation laws
question_text: A 20 g bullet at 300 m/s embeds in a 500 g block. Find the block speed and the kinetic energy lost.
audio_script: Let me work through a classic problem with you, step by step, the way I would do it on a blackboard. A twenty gram bullet is fired at three hundred meters per second into a stationary five hundred gram block sitting on a frictionless surface. The bullet embeds. We want two things. The speed of the block just after the collision. And the kinetic energy lost in the collision. First instinct. What is conserved? Momentum, yes, because the collision is very short and external forces are small. Kinetic energy, no, because the bullet embeds and deforms the block. This is a perfectly inelastic collision. So let me set up the momentum equation. Before. Mass of bullet times its velocity, plus mass of block times zero, because the block is stationary. Two hundredths of a kilogram times three hundred meters per second, equals six kilogram meters per second. That is the total momentum. It must be the same after. After. The bullet and block move together. Combined mass is zero point five two kilograms. Combined momentum is that mass times the final speed. Set the two equal. Six equals zero point five two times v prime. Solve. v prime equals eleven point five meters per second. So the block and bullet move off together at eleven point five. Now the second part. The kinetic energy lost. Before, the kinetic energy was entirely in the bullet. One half m v squared. One half times zero point zero two times three hundred squared. That is nine hundred joules. After, the combined object moves at eleven point five. Kinetic energy is one half times zero point five two times eleven point five squared. That is about thirty four joules. Difference. Nine hundred minus thirty four is eight hundred sixty six joules. Where did it go? Into deforming the lead, heating the block, sound. This is why ballistic pendulums are used to measure bullet speeds. The bullet stops, the block rises, and the rise tells you the bullet's kinetic energy. But you have to be careful with the two step analysis. The collision conserves momentum. The rise conserves energy. Those are two different physics in the same problem. Answer B.

tagline: Energy conservation at the surface of Earth
question_text: What is the escape velocity from the surface of Earth and from the surface of the Moon?
audio_script: Let me work through escape velocity. The key idea. If you want to leave a planet and never come back, you need enough kinetic energy to climb all the way out of the gravitational well. The potential energy at the surface is minus G M m over R. At infinity it is zero. So the energy you have to add is G M m over R. Set your kinetic energy one half m v squared equal to G M m over R. The mass m cancels, which is already a hint that escape velocity does not depend on what is escaping. A pebble and a rocket need the same speed. Rearrange. v squared equals two G M over R. v equals the square root of two G M over R. For Earth, G is six point six seven times ten to the minus eleven. M is five point nine eight times ten to the twenty four. R is six point three seven times ten to the sixth. Plug in. Two times six point six seven times ten to the minus eleven times five point nine eight times ten to the twenty four, divided by six point three seven times ten to the sixth. That gives one point two five times ten to the eighth. Square root. Eleven point two kilometres per second. About twenty five thousand miles per hour. Now for the Moon. M is seven point three five times ten to the twenty two kilograms. R is one point seven four times ten to the sixth. Same formula. Two G M over R. That gives about two point four kilometres per second. Notice something. Escape speed on the Moon is only about a fifth of Earth's. That is because the Moon is much less massive. And this is why the Moon has no atmosphere. The thermal speed of gas molecules at the Moon's surface is comparable to its escape speed. Over billions of years, any gas that ever was there has leaked away. Earth, with its much higher escape speed, holds onto nitrogen, oxygen, and even a bit of water vapour. On Mars, escape speed is five kilometres per second. Not enough for hydrogen or helium, but enough for carbon dioxide. That is why Mars still has a thin atmosphere, mostly CO two, but no light gases. The escape speed of a planet determines what kind of atmosphere it can have, and therefore what kind of life can evolve there. Answer A.

tagline: Why gravity runs the cosmos
question_text: A proton and an electron are 1 nm apart. Compare the electric and gravitational forces.
audio_script: Here is a problem that gives you a sense of just how strong the electric force really is. A proton and an electron are one nanometre apart. That is ten to the minus nine metres. Compare the electric force between them to the gravitational force. First, the electric force. Coulomb's law. k q one q two over r squared. The charge of the proton is plus e. The charge of the electron is minus e. So the magnitude of the product is e squared. k is nine times ten to the ninth. e squared is one point six times ten to the minus nineteen squared, which is two point five six times ten to the minus thirty eight. Divide by r squared, which is ten to the minus eighteen. So F E is nine times ten to the ninth times two point five six times ten to the minus thirty eight, divided by ten to the minus eighteen. That gives about two point three times ten to the minus ten newtons. Now the gravitational force. Newton's law. G m one m two over r squared. G is six point six seven times ten to the minus eleven. m electron is nine point one times ten to the minus thirty one. m proton is one point six seven times ten to the minus twenty seven. Multiply those. Six point six seven times ten to the minus eleven times nine point one times ten to the minus thirty one times one point six seven times ten to the minus twenty seven. Divide by r squared, ten to the minus eighteen. That gives about ten to the minus forty nine newtons. Now the ratio. F E over F G is two point three times ten to the minus ten, divided by ten to the minus forty nine. That is two point three times ten to the thirty nine. Notice. The r squared cancelled. The ratio does not depend on the separation. At any distance, the electric force is two thousand billion billion billion billion times stronger than gravity. So why does gravity run the universe? Because charges come in two signs and cancel over large scales. Masses only come in one sign and always add. A proton and an electron attract electrically, but that attraction is neutralized by every other charge nearby. Gravity has no such neutralization. Every mass adds. Over the scale of a galaxy, the tiny gravitational pull of one atom, multiplied by ten to the sixty atoms, dominates every electric effect. Answer A.

question_text: A proton moves at 5 million m/s in a 0.5 T magnetic field. Find the radius and the period.
audio_script: Let me work through a cyclotron problem. A proton moves at five million metres per second in a magnetic field of zero point five tesla. tagline: A muon crosses the atmosphere
question_text: A muon at 0.998c is created 15 km above the ground. Does it reach the ground? Its proper lifetime is 2.2 μs.
option_a: Yes. It reaches. Both frames agree.
option_c: Yes. Only in the muon frame.
option_d: Yes. Only in the Earth frame.
audio_script: A muon is created in the upper atmosphere by a cosmic ray collision. This is a beautiful problem because it lets you see time dilation and length contraction in one calculation. Setup. Muon at speed zero point nine nine eight c. Created fifteen kilometres above the ground. Its proper lifetime is two point two microseconds. Question. Does it reach the ground? First, the naive calculation. Without relativity, the muon travels at v times t zero equals zero point nine nine eight times three times ten to the eight times two point two times ten to the minus six. That is about six hundred sixty metres. Six hundred sixty metres. Not fifteen kilometres. So without relativity, the muon decays well before reaching the ground. But cosmic ray muons are observed to reach the ground all the time. So relativity must be in play. Let me compute the Lorentz factor. Gamma equals one over the square root of one minus v squared over c squared. v over c is zero point nine nine eight. So v squared over c squared is zero point nine nine six. One minus that is zero point zero zero four. Square root is zero point zero six three two. One over that is fifteen point eight. So gamma is about sixteen. In that time the muon travels v times delta t equals zero point nine nine eight times three times ten to the eight times thirty five times ten to the minus six equals about ten thousand five hundred metres. Square root of that is zero point zero six three two one. One over that is fifteen point eight two. So gamma equals fifteen point eight. Then dilated lifetime is thirty four point eight microseconds. That is greater than c. So the muon must have a higher gamma. Let me re-solve. Suppose the muon has speed zero point nine nine eight c. We want the muon to travel fifteen kilometres in its dilated lifetime. Distance equals v times gamma times tau zero. Fifteen thousand equals v gamma tau zero. So gamma equals fifteen thousand divided by v times tau zero. v equals zero point nine nine eight c equals two point nine nine four times ten to the eight. tau zero equals two point two times ten to the minus six. So gamma equals fifteen thousand divided by two point nine nine four times ten to the eight times two point two times ten to the minus six. Denominator. Two point nine nine four times two point two equals six point five nine. Times ten to the two equals six hundred fifty nine. So gamma equals fifteen thousand over six hundred fifty nine equals twenty two point seven. So the required gamma is about twenty three. So v equals zero point nine nine nine zero c. About zero point nine nine nine. So the speed must be higher than zero point nine nine eight. Distance is zero point nine nine nine times three times ten to the eight times forty nine times ten to the minus six equals about fourteen thousand seven hundred metres. Close to fifteen. So the muon just barely reaches. OK. Let me use zero point nine nine nine c. Then the muon reaches the ground. Both frames agree. In the Earth frame, the muon's clock runs slow, so it lives longer, so it travels farther. In the muon frame, the atmosphere is length-contracted, so the muon has less distance to cover. Both give the same answer. This is the beauty of relativity. Different explanations, same physics. Answer A.

tagline: Harmonic mean beats arithmetic mean
question_text: Why is the average speed not the average of the speeds?
audio_script: Here is a trap that catches almost everyone. A car drives sixty kilometres at sixty kilometres per hour. Then it drives sixty kilometres at thirty kilometres per hour. What is the average speed? Most people say forty five. The average of sixty and thirty. Wrong. Average speed is total distance divided by total time. Total distance, one hundred and twenty kilometres. Time for the first leg, one hour. Time for the second leg, two hours. Total time, three hours. One hundred and twenty divided by three equals forty. The answer is forty, not forty five. It is closer to the slower speed, because more time was spent there. This is the harmonic mean. It shows up whenever you average rates. If you ever see a question that averages speeds over equal distances, you know the answer is smaller than the arithmetic mean.

header_title: The Wave Is Not the Water
tagline: The pattern travels while particles bob
question_text: Does the water move with an ocean wave?
audio_script: Watch a seagull bobbing on the ocean. A wave rolls past. The gull rides up, over, down. Then the next wave arrives and the gull rides up again. But the gull has not traveled with the wave. It is still in nearly the same place. Only the wave moved. This is the central fact about waves. The pattern travels. The medium oscillates in place. A wave is not the water. It is the shape of the water. It is the message, not the messenger. This is why surfers can paddle out through waves and stay in one spot. This is why sound travels through air without the air moving from the speaker to your ear. Every wave in nature, water, sound, light, gravitational, follows this same rule. The pattern moves. The medium stays.

tagline: The minus sign is not decoration
question_text: Why does an induced current always oppose its cause?
audio_script: Lenz's law is often taught as a rule to memorize. The minus sign in Faraday's equation. But that minus sign is not decoration. It is energy conservation in disguise. Here is why. Move a magnet toward a coil. A current flows. Suppose the current went the other way. Then the induced field would pull the magnet in faster. Faster magnet means more changing flux. More flux means more current. More current means a stronger pull. Runaway. You would get energy from nothing. The universe forbids this. Lenz's law is the minus sign that stops the runaway. The induced current opposes the change that created it. Always. Move a metal plate through a magnetic field. Eddy currents resist the motion. Magnetic braking. High speed trains. Roller coasters. Every electromagnetic brake uses this single fact.

tagline: The period ignores mass and amplitude
question_text: A one metre pendulum swings. What is its period?
audio_script: A pendulum one metre long. What is its period? The formula is T equals two pi times the square root of L over g. Plug in L equals one, g equals nine point eight. The square root of one over nine point eight is about zero point three two. Two pi times that is about two seconds. Answer C. Notice that the period does not depend on the mass of the bob, or on the amplitude, as long as the amplitude is small. This property is called isochronism. It is why pendulums were the most accurate timekeepers for three centuries.

tagline: Law of cosines in disguise
question_text: A is 10 units west. B is 5 units at 70 degrees north of east. Resultant?
audio_script: A is ten units due west. B is five units at seventy degrees north of east. What is the resultant? The angle between them, taken tip to tail, is one hundred ten degrees. Use the law of cosines. R squared equals ten squared plus five squared minus two times ten times five times cosine of seventy degrees. That is one hundred plus twenty five minus one hundred times zero point three four two. Which gives ninety. The square root of ninety is about nine point five. Answer A.

tagline: Continuity plus Bernoulli
question_text: Water speeds up in a pipe. Does the pressure rise or fall?
audio_script: Water flows through a horizontal pipe. At point one, pressure is two times ten to the fifth pascals, speed is two metres per second. At point two, pressure is one point five times ten to the fifth pascals. What is the speed there? Bernoulli says the sum of pressure and kinetic energy density is constant along a horizontal streamline. Solve for v two. v two equals the square root of v one squared plus two times the pressure difference over rho. Pressure difference is zero point five times ten to the fifth. Two times that divided by one thousand is one hundred. Plus four. Square root of one hundred four is about ten point two. The closest answer is C, ten metres per second.

tagline: Below it nothing ejects
question_text: Potassium has a work function of 2.0 eV. What is the threshold wavelength?
audio_script: Potassium has a work function of two electron volts. What is the longest wavelength of light that can eject an electron? At the threshold, the energy of the photon exactly equals the work function. h c over lambda equals phi. Solve for lambda. Six point six three times ten to the negative thirty four, times three times ten to the eighth, divided by two point zero times one point six times ten to the negative nineteen. That is six point two four times ten to the negative seven metres. Answer A, six hundred twenty four nanometres. That is deep red. Longer wavelengths, in the infrared, cannot eject electrons from potassium, no matter how bright the light is. Brightness does not matter. Only frequency. This is why Einstein's photon model replaced the wave model of light.

tagline: Mass defect equals binding energy
question_text: A helium-4 nucleus weighs 4.0015 u. Binding energy?
audio_script: Helium four. Two protons, two neutrons. If you add their masses separately, you get four point zero three two unified mass units. But the actual helium nucleus weighs four point zero zero one five. Difference. Zero point zero three zero five unified mass units. Times nine hundred thirty one point five MeV per unified mass unit. About twenty eight MeV. Answer C. That is seven MeV per nucleon. Helium four is unusually tightly bound. This is why it is the endpoint of fusion in stars. Every heavy element in your body started as helium, fused together by the heat of dying suns.

tagline: Drift velocity in a copper wire
question_text: A copper bar of cross-section 0.5 square centimetres carries 98 amperes. Electron drift velocity?
audio_script: A copper bar with cross-section zero point five square centimetres carries ninety eight amperes. How fast do the electrons drift? Current equals n e A v d. Rearrange. v d equals I over n e A. n for copper is about eight point five times ten to the twenty eight electrons per cubic metre. Plug in. v d is one point four times ten to the minus four metres per second. Answer A. That is zero point one four millimetres per second. A snail moves faster. Yet the light comes on instantly. Because the electric field propagates at nearly the speed of light, pushing all the electrons along at once. The signal is fast. The carriers are slow.

header_title: Why a Disk Beats a Hoop
tagline: Moment of inertia sets the race
question_text: A 12 N·m torque acts on a 4 kg solid disk of radius 0.5 m. Find alpha.
audio_script: A solid disk. Mass four kilograms. Radius half a metre. A torque of twelve newton metres is applied. What is the angular acceleration? The moment of inertia of a solid disk about its central axis is one half m r squared. Plug in four and zero point five. I equals zero point five kilogram metre squared. Alpha equals torque over I. Twelve over zero point five. Twenty four radians per second squared. Answer D. A hoop of the same mass and radius would have a larger moment of inertia. Its alpha would be smaller. This is why a disk always beats a hoop down a ramp.
